title: ASCENT-Load: An Open-Source BDF-Native Aeroelastic and Rotor Loads Framework for Certification-Oriented eVTOL Loads Analysis
description:
ASCENT-Load is an open-source aeroelastic finite-element and loads-analysis framework that reads and writes MSC Nastran bulk-data (BDF) input and integrates fixed-wing static aeroelastic trim (SOL 144, with inertia relief for free-free models) with rotor load models for hover, transition, and rotor-failure cases in a single tested certification-oriented loads pipeline. It is developed at the ASCENT Laboratory (structures), Department of Aerospace Engineering, Inha University.

The aeroelastic coupling uses a two-G-matrix spline that separates the normalwash and force-transfer roles. Trim is reduced by a Schur complement onto the trim degrees of freedom, so subcases sharing a flight condition reuse one factorization. Rotor loads from blade-element momentum theory and a reduced-order Pitt-Peters-form inflow lag feed the same finite-element model and the load-recovery, V-M-T envelope, and critical-design-load pipeline, ending in FORCE/MOMENT design-load decks. Solution sequences implemented and covered by the test suite are SOL 101, SOL 103, and SOL 144; SOL 145 (flutter) and SOL 146 are not implemented.

This release (version 1.5.0, tag v1.5-paper1) accompanies the submitted manuscripts. The project was previously released under the name NastAero; the new name identifies the developing laboratory, and code, history, and results are unchanged by the rename. The Python package is ascent_load, the commands are ascent-load and ascent-load-gui, and result archives use the .aload extension (older .naero archives still load without conversion).

The test suite is run in continuous integration on every change, on Python 3.10 and 3.12. It comprises 1031 automated tests. A public clone reports 1005 passed and 26 skipped with the optional GUI extra installed, and 981 collected / 955 passed / 26 skipped without it, because the 51 GUI tests are not collected when that extra is absent. The skipped tests require a third-party proprietary comparison aircraft model that is not redistributable and is therefore excluded from this archive; with that data present the suite reports 1031 passed.
